newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian electricity futures to help market - SFE.
newsitem.headline: Australian electricity futures to help market - SFE.

text.p: The listing of two electricity contracts on the Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) on September 29 will help achieve the competition objectives of the national electricity market, SFE chief executive Les Hosking said.
Deregulation, corporatisation and privatisation in the electricity industry has raised risk management as a key issue for market participants, Hosking said in a statement on Monday.
"Sustainable profitability for organisations operating in the electricity industry will depend heavily on risk management using tools such as futures contracts," he said.
A futures market in electricity also would help participants access readily available publicly disseminated quotations for current and forward prices of electricity, he said.
Such transparency of price information would greatly assist the cornerstone objective of a national electricity market in creating a competitive wholesale market, he said.
Futures markets reduced price risk, which resulted in lower electricity prices for all consumers while ensuring sustainable profitability for generators and retail distributors, he said.
The electricity futures contracts, based on Victorian and New South Wales electricity markets, would trade each business day on SFE's screen dealing system SYCOM, he said.
Each contract will equal 500 megawatt hours of electricity and will be quoted for each month up to 12 months ahead.

"SYCOM provides an ideal environment for these new contracts as market participants currently use this electronic trading platform for the electricity futures contracts traded in Australia on the link with the New York Mercantile Exchange and for the New Zealand Futures and Options Exchange," he said.
The contracts will be the first electricity futures for Australia and mark a significant development in the transformation of the Australian electricity industry, he said.
